claims.text: PSA screening = controversial and should involve shared decision-making.
claims.quote: Screening is controversial and should involve shared decision-making.

claims.text: Who = screened: commonly men 45 to 75, earlier @ ↑risk (FHx, Black men, germline mutations); USU ⍉w life expectancy < 10 to 15 years or age over 75.
claims.quote: Screening recommendations can vary, but screening is commonly done annually or biannually in men between 45 and 75 years old and is sometimes begun earlier for men at high risk (eg, those with a family history of prostate cancer, Black men, men with germline mutations). Screening is not usually recommended for men with a life expectancy < 10 to 15 years or men older than age 75.

claims.text: An ↑PSA = ⍉diagnostic: infect or prostate enlrg can raise it too.
claims.quote: An elevated PSA may be suggestive of cancer but can also occur with infection or prostate enlargement and is not therefore definitively diagnostic of prostate cancer.

claims.text: After an abnorm result: multiparametric MRI and urine or blood tests help decide on bx; bx = the only way to diagnose prostate CA.
claims.quote: Abnormal findings are further investigated based on clinician and patient preferences. Multiparametric MRI can detect suspect lesions, and various urine and blood tests may help risk stratification of a patient's need for prostate biopsy. Ultimately, however, a prostate biopsy remains the only way to diagnose prostate cancer.
